text: The Port Authority bus system in Pittsburgh gets a lot of attention. Some of that attention is deserved, because the network does cover many neighborhoods that would otherwise be hard to reach without a car. On the other hand, the buses are frequently late, and the real-time tracking in the app is not always accurate. During rush hour, it’s normal to see buses packed to the point where riders have to stand in the aisles for the entire trip. Outside of peak times, though, the gaps between buses can be so long that missing one means being stuck for nearly an hour. The drivers are generally professional and courteous, which helps offset some of the frustration with the schedule. Fares are reasonable compared to ride-sharing, but the cost can add up for daily commuters, especially when transfers are needed. Some routes are designed thoughtfully, with limited stops that make cross-town trips relatively quick. Others feel outdated and winding, forcing riders to take long, indirect journeys to reach common destinations. If the Port Authority invested more in frequency, reliability, and clearer route information, the system could go from merely functional to truly excellent. For now, it remains a mixed experience: essential for many residents, but far from as efficient or user-friendly as it could be.

text: We arrived a bit early for our reservation and they were able to seat us right away. Even with a fairly packed dining room, the place wasn't too loud. If you have any old people in your group, they can seat you downstairs as I don't think they have an elevator (I prefer being upstairs overlooking looking the dining room, it's a nice touch). The Lobster Arancini were cooked perfectly with no crunchy, undercooked risotto inside. The only downside was that there were just 3 (we had 4 people) and they were tiny so it was almost impossible to split them. As for entrees, the gnocchi topped with a duck ragu are a fantastic dish, not too rich and the gnocchi simply melt in your mouth. The Zuppa di Pesce has a wonderfully balanced broth which wasn't oversalted (a surprise given the amount of shellfish) and tasted like it might have had Sherry wine in it. I think I counted 7 or 8 different items in this seafood hodgepodge. As for service, it was quite good and we were done with 3 courses in a bit over an hour. Lidia's certainly ranks up there as one of my favorite Italian restaurants in the city.

text: I've been to Lidia's a few times before and figured I'd leave a review after today's trip. The atmosphere is consistently warm and inviting, with that authentic Italian charm that makes you feel like you're dining in someone's home. Our server was attentive without being overbearing, checking in at just the right moments throughout our meal. I started with the antipasto platter, which was generously portioned and featured high-quality cured meats and perfectly ripe tomatoes. For my main course, I ordered the osso buco, and it was absolutely tender and flavorful - the meat practically fell off the bone. My dining companion had the homemade pappardelle with wild boar ragu, which she couldn't stop raving about. The wine selection is impressive, and our server helped us choose a Chianti that paired beautifully with our dishes. The prices are reasonable for the quality and portion sizes you receive. The only minor complaint would be that it can get quite loud when the restaurant is full, making conversation a bit challenging. Overall, Lidia's continues to deliver an excellent dining experience, and I'll definitely be returning soon.

text: How does this place get so highly rated on Yelp? It's not awful, but it was one of the most mediocre brick-oven pizzas I've ever eaten. S. This is yet another Pittsburgh establishment that doesn't take credit cards. Seriously, is the whole city in a 1995 time warp? (.. . Or are all of these places just cheating on their tax bills? text: WTF? I just finished this movie and I'm sitting here completely stunned by what I just witnessed. This has to be one of the most bizarre and inexplicable films I've ever encountered in my entire life. The plot makes absolutely no sense whatsoever, jumping from scene to scene without any logical connection or coherent narrative structure. The dialogue sounds like it was written by someone who has never heard actual human beings speak to each other. I kept waiting for some kind of explanation or revelation that would tie everything together, but it never came. The acting ranges from wooden to completely over-the-top, with no middle ground or natural performances anywhere to be found. text: I do agree with most of the reviews that OG isn't in my top 10 places that I care to dine. The breadsticks, while unlimited, are often overcooked and lack the buttery flavor they're supposed to have. Service tends to be inconsistent - sometimes you get a server who's attentive and friendly, other times you feel completely forgotten. The pasta portions are generous, I'll give them that, but the sauces taste like they come straight from a jar without much enhancement. Their salad is probably the most reliable item on the menu, though it's hard to mess up lettuce and Italian dressing. The atmosphere tries to feel authentic Italian but ends up feeling more like a themed chain restaurant. Prices have gone up significantly over the years while the quality seems to have stayed the same or declined. The wait times can be ridiculous, especially on weekends, for what is essentially fast-casual Italian food. Their chicken dishes are particularly disappointing - often dry and lacking seasoning. The wine selection is limited and overpriced for what you get. Parking can be a nightmare at most locations during peak hours. The desserts are clearly not made in-house and taste like frozen selections you could buy at the grocery store. Kids seem to enjoy it, which I suppose is the target demographic they're going for. The restaurant is always loud and chaotic, making conversation difficult. Overall, it's not terrible, but there are so many better Italian options available for the same price point.

text: Bagels, in my opinion, are one of the best breakfast alternatives to actually sitting down to a nice breakfast. No.. . these bagels are about the same you would get anywhere. Just as chewy, that taste of "this is feigning fresh because it is warm and was just heated up, but it's definitely not fresh fresh. "nSadly, this is what Pittsburghers must settle for. I we can hope for is that one day a kind Philadelphian or New Yorker will show us the light, and bring us light, fluffy bagels of my dreams!

text: It is rather unfortunate that Pittsburgh doesn't have ANY privately owned strictly bagel joints. The city seems to rely heavily on chain establishments and grocery store bakeries for what they call "bagels," but these mass-produced rounds of bread barely deserve the name. A real bagel should have that perfect chewy texture with a slightly crispy exterior that can only be achieved through traditional boiling and baking methods. Instead, what we get here are these soft, doughy circles that taste more like hamburger buns shaped into rings. I've lived in cities with authentic bagel culture, and the difference is night and day. The cream cheese selection at most places is limited to basic flavors, nothing like the variety you'd find at a proper bagel shop. Even the everything seasoning seems sparse and flavorless compared to what I'm used to. It's particularly disappointing given Pittsburgh's rich food culture in other areas - we have amazing pierogi, great sandwich shops, and fantastic pizza joints.
label: llm

text: nnI had a bad impression of this hotel before I even entered. I made a two-night reservation for a business trip, but I was stranded in an airport overnight because of cancelled flights. text: Despite being a Marriott-brand hotel, Courtyard Pittsburgh Downtown's service and room qualities were not up to par with the Marriott standard but still charged Marriott price. text: This pizza is certainly edible, but it is not at the top of my pizza-scale, a place reserved for the Grimaldis and Lombardis of the world (or, more realistically, just the U.S. ; Italian pizza, I have heard and trust, is even better). nnFiori's is just underwhelming. Service was helpful, friendly, and quick. But the pizza just fell flat. The sauce was so sweet, which is not normal outside of this region (not sure what sweet tomato sauce is about, but I don't dig it. There has to be sugar added or something. ). Dough was ok but wasn't that perfect medium for the simple yet magical tomato and mozzarella combination that it ought to be. If you are expecting New York style pizza, this is NOT the place for you. Average at best, but better than your fast-food pizza places if you are in a pinch. For me, that will be never.

text: First I must clarify that my rating here is based on my scale of pizza-ratings only. Within that context, this place delivers a solid, respectable pie that hits most of the marks I look for. The crust strikes a nice balance between crispy and chewy, with just enough char on the bottom to show it was properly fired. Their sauce has a good tomato-forward flavor without being overly sweet or acidic, though it could use a touch more seasoning. The cheese blend melts beautifully and doesn't create that greasy puddle you sometimes get with lower-quality mozzarella. I tried their pepperoni pizza, and the meat had a nice spice level with good cup-and-char action. The portion sizes are generous - two slices here will fill you up more than three slices at most chain places. Service was efficient, and my pizza came out hot within the promised timeframe. The dining area is clean and has that classic New York pizzeria atmosphere without trying too hard. Pricing is fair for the quality and portion size you're getting. My only real complaint is that the crust could have used another minute in the oven for my personal preference. The garlic knots I ordered as a side were perfectly seasoned and not too oily. Overall, while this isn't going to revolutionize your pizza experience, it's exactly what you want from a neighborhood pizza joint.
label: llm

text: First off, it is desperately in need of some updates. There are old crappy projector screens and a few big rear projection TVs, but not an HDTV in sight. You mean I could go to my hotel to watch the game but am unable to watch it at a "sports bar"?? Give me a break. nnFood is also generally terrible. Nachos are no better than what you can get at 7-11 and sandwiches have no flavor. And service is piss poor and understaffed. I'm not sure if they recently changed ownership or what, but something was very very off here and they were obviously unprepared for the start of the football season. nnI feel bad because the people were very nice and apologetic, but that does not take away from the fact that even if they were showing my game, I think I'd still rather watch it in my hotel room.

text: The screens are outdated and constantly flickering, making it nearly impossible to follow the action during crucial moments of the game. The seating arrangement is poorly planned, with obstructed views from multiple angles and chairs that look like they were salvaged from a closing restaurant. Staff members seem completely disinterested in providing any level of customer service, often ignoring requests or taking an unreasonably long time to bring orders. The food menu is limited and overpriced for what amounts to basic bar food that tastes like it's been sitting under heat lamps for hours. Even basic amenities like clean restrooms and adequate lighting seem to be too much to ask for at this establishment. The atmosphere feels more like a run-down dive bar than a proper sports viewing venue. Other similar places in the area have embraced modern technology with crystal-clear HD displays and surround sound systems that make you feel like you're at the stadium. The management here seems content to coast on whatever reputation they might have had years ago rather than making necessary improvements.

text: La Pomponnee, I wanted to like you. The charming French name and elegant storefront drew me in with promises of authentic Parisian bistro dining. text: That designation usually means fancy Chinese food at high-end prices. Even in Boston and Chicago, $30 was a lot for an entree. text: Pan-Asian fusion. This restaurant takes bold culinary risks that largely pay off in exciting and unexpected ways. The menu seamlessly weaves together flavors from Thailand, Japan, Korea, and Vietnam, creating dishes that feel both familiar and refreshingly innovative. Their signature ramen bowl combines traditional Japanese tonkotsu broth with Korean kimchi and Thai basil, resulting in a complex umami bomb that keeps you coming back for more. The Korean BBQ tacos are another standout, featuring perfectly marinated bulgogi beef wrapped in house-made tortillas with pickled daikon and sriracha aioli. The sushi rolls push creative boundaries without sacrificing quality, particularly the "Bangkok Roll" which incorporates massaman curry powder and fresh mango. Service is attentive and knowledgeable, with servers happy to explain the cultural inspirations behind each dish. The atmosphere strikes an elegant balance between modern sophistication and casual comfort. Exposed brick walls are adorned with contemporary Asian artwork, while soft lighting creates an intimate dining environment.
label: llm

text: Sports bars. There's something undeniably magnetic about these establishments that combines the thrill of athletic competition with the social atmosphere of a neighborhood gathering place. What sets exceptional sports bars apart from mediocre ones is attention to the viewing experience. The best establishments invest in high-quality, large-screen televisions with crystal-clear picture quality that makes you feel like you're sitting courtside or on the fifty-yard line. Strategic seating arrangements ensure that no matter where you sit, you have an unobstructed view of at least two or three screens. The lighting is carefully calibrated to reduce glare while maintaining enough brightness to read menus and navigate safely. The food menu at a quality sports bar strikes a delicate balance between comfort food classics and more sophisticated offerings. Sure, you expect excellent wings, loaded nachos, and perfectly seasoned burgers, but the standout venues also offer surprises like gourmet flatbreads, fresh salads, and creative appetizers that go beyond typical bar fare. The kitchen needs to handle the rush of halftime orders while maintaining consistency and quality throughout busy game days. Beer selection often defines a sports bar's personality and clientele. Draft beer should be served ice-cold in properly chilled glasses, with taps that are regularly cleaned and maintained.

The green curry is a standout dish that delivers an authentic heat level that builds gradually, allowing you to appreciate the complex layers of coconut milk, Thai eggplant, and aromatic herbs. What impressed me most was their som tam salad, which featured perfectly julienned green papaya with a dressing that captured that essential Thai flavor profile of fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar. The mango sticky rice dessert was the ideal finale, with perfectly ripe mango slices paired with coconut-infused sticky rice that wasn't overly sweet. Portion sizes are generous without being overwhelming, and the presentation of each dish shows clear attention to detail and pride in their craft. The spice levels are accurately represented on the menu, so you can order with confidence whether you prefer mild or authentically fiery heat. Their tom yum soup delivers that perfect sour and spicy punch that clears your sinuses while warming your soul. The restaurant maintains consistently high quality across multiple visits, which speaks to their kitchen's skill and dedication to authentic preparation methods.

I was looking for the salty little slivers of love with some crisp! nnService wasn't super inviting and the cash register attendant didn't even hint at a smile when we ordered. As soon as cash was in hand, she went back to her computer - adjacent to the counter. With a sanitation score barely above 90 and the flavorless eats, I have indeed experienced some better burger joints in the QC.
label: human

text: We decided on a small, candlelit bistro that had recently opened in the heart of the downtown area. As soon as we walked through the door, the aroma of garlic and fresh herbs greeted us warmly. The hostess was incredibly welcoming and led us to a cozy corner booth that felt quite intimate. We started by ordering two signature cocktails that were as refreshing as the unusual breeze outside. For an appetizer, we chose the crispy Brussels sprouts drizzled with a balsamic reduction and topped with pancetta. The crunch was perfect, and the flavor profile hit all the right notes of salty and sweet. Our server, a knowledgeable young man named Marcus, gave us excellent recommendations for our main courses. Hubs opted for the pan-seared scallops, which arrived beautifully plated on a bed of creamy risotto. I decided on the homemade pappardelle pasta tossed in a rich, slow-cooked short rib ragu. The pasta was perfectly al dente, and the meat was so tender it practically melted in my mouth. We shared a side of garlic mashed potatoes that were decadent enough to be a meal on their own. Throughout the evening, the pacing of the meal was spot on, giving us plenty of time to chat without feeling rushed. The ambient music was soft enough to allow for easy conversation yet loud enough to provide a nice backdrop. Even though we were quite full, Marcus convinced us to take a look at the dessert menu.
label: llm

text: You know that going on. You're probably going to feel a little sick or regretful after your meal. You know that going in, too. But still, this place makes the tastiest, worst food. I can't help but go back time and time again, even if it's just to reward myself for good behavior. nnThere's a lot to love about Bojangles, this location in particular. As you'd expect, this location is super clean and, well, pretty fast; you get your food in a timely fashion, which makes the crowds less intimidating. The fries are to die for: supremely seasoned and pipin' hot. My girlfriend lives and dies by Bojangles biscuits, so be sure to grab one if you can. While their chicken sandwiches are awesome, I love their tenders too; I often combine these with a meal of mashed potatoes and/or slaw. nnAgain, probably the least healthy option in the world, but as far as fast food--what a tasty option.
label: human

text: But you don't go there to count calories; you go there because your soul needs grease and carbs. The Cajun Filet Biscuit is a masterpiece of spice and sodium that makes your heart flutter for all the wrong reasons. I usually pair it with a side of Bo-Rounds, those crispy potato discs that are perfectly salted and strangely addictive. The breading on the chicken has just enough kick to wake up your taste buds without ruining your morning. And let's talk about the sweet tea, which is essentially liquid sugar with a hint of tea leaves. It is the kind of drink that could probably power a small engine, yet I find myself ordering a large every single time. If you still have room after the main course, you absolutely cannot skip the Bo-Berry Biscuit. That warm, blueberry-filled dough covered in a thick icing is the ultimate sugary reward. Sure, the drive-thru line might be wrapped around the building on a Sunday morning, but the wait is always worth it.
label: llm

text: My girlfriends and I thoroughly enjoy the half-price martinis on Wednesdays - my personal fave is the pineapple upside-down martini. Mmmm tastes like cake! Who doesn't like cake in a glass? nnI've eaten a variety of dishes on the menu and each dish I've had was both tasty and affordable enough to come back. Some of my favorites are the Fried Goat Cheese Salad, the Shepherd Pizza and Pasta Primavera. nnFor those adult beverage seekers, the bar can get crowded during happy hour and special event evenings. I'm a fan of Cosmo's bar crowd, as compared to its neighbors, this bar attracts a well behaved crowd of upper 20s-late 30s. Not that I have an issue with a younger crowd, but I'm just jiving with the cages, swings and go-go dancers next door. nnMake sure to note that Cosmo's sports a limited menu on big event nights and offers half price apps from 5-7 pm. This is definitely a spot to make reservations during event nights!
label: human

text: The service is consistently quick, which is essential when you're on a tight schedule. They offer an extensive menu that caters to almost any craving, ranging from hearty burgers to fresh, crisp salads. I usually opt for the classic cheeseburger deluxe, which always arrives hot and seasoned just right. The portions are generous enough to keep you full through a long performance without feeling overly weighed down. Even during the pre-theater rush, the atmosphere remains lively and welcoming rather than stressful. The staff is incredibly efficient and seems to have a professional knack for keeping things moving smoothly. It’s a huge relief to find a spot in this part of town where you can get a full meal without breaking the bank. The booths are comfortable, providing a nice little oasis of calm away from the busy city streets outside. Whether you’re a local or just visiting for a show, it’s a reliable staple that consistently delivers on quality.
label: llm

text: They set us all up in a hotel not too far from the airport so that was great.. . until we read the yelp reviews that the place is stinky, not clean and had bed bugs. We figured we would try it out so we called for the shuttle to come to pick us up because we had no place to stay. We sat out in the cold for 40 min when we were told it would take 15 min by hotel staff that helped us. Cold and exhausted we went back into the airport to see if there was another option. Nope. Finally after another 15-20 minutes the shuttle came and we drove to the hotel. When we got to our rooms one wreaked of smoke and had multiple hair strands (that weren't ours) on the made up beds. We walked into the other room which smelled better but had a huge beetle crawling on the wall, spider in the bed, crumbs on the night stand, hairs and dirt in the shower, and hairs and urine on the toilet. We were 5 girls that are stuck in a disgusting hotel at 12 AM, on the opposite coast. All the other hotels either full or ridiculously expensive and United would not get back to us. I will never be flying with them again. nnnOh and to top it off when we got back to California we found another person last year that we know had the same thing happen to her except she slept in the bed, got bed bugs on her face and ended up going to the emergency room because of the reaction. I wish I could give them zero stars. This place is DISGUSTING. Don't ever stay there.
label: human

text: We were stranded at Charlotte Douglas International Airport for what felt like an eternity while trying to speak with a gate agent. The lines at the customer service desk were wrapping around the terminal, filled with hundreds of other exhausted passengers. After waiting for three hours, we finally reached a representative who seemed completely overwhelmed by the situation. She informed us that there were no available flights to Los Angeles for the next forty-eight hours. To make matters worse, the airline refused to provide any vouchers for a hotel or even basic meal discounts. My friends and I had to scramble on our phones to find a decent place to stay that wouldn't break the bank. We eventually found a small motel twenty minutes away from the airport, but the shuttle service was non-existent. The Uber ride for the five of us with all our luggage ended up costing nearly eighty dollars. The next morning, we returned to the airport early, hoping for a miracle on the standby list. We spent the entire day sitting on the floor near the gate because every single seat in the terminal was occupied. Communication from the airline was virtually nonexistent, as the app kept giving us conflicting information about our status. It wasn't until late that evening that a sympathetic supervisor finally took notice of our group. He managed to find five seats on a red-eye flight that connected through Phoenix before finally heading to LAX.
label: llm

text: nnBut it is one of the oldest punk/hardcore/metal/rock venues in Charlotte, and legend has it that Nirvana played there WAY back in the day. nnIt is sort of an assault on your senses. Visually, the band sticker/graffiti decor can keep you entertained with all the random bands that have played there. The music is going to be loud enough to leave your ears ringing in the packed little stage room. In the summer months, you can tell that the power bill is not high because of air conditioning. This not only turns everyone into a sweaty mess, but it makes the bathrooms an olfactory gauntlet. They are also pretty lax on the no smoking policy. nnThe PBR tallboys are cold as most bands can tell you since I have seen more than one act showered in beer by the moshing crowd. nnMake sure you bring cash unless you care to deal with their less than comforting ATM behind the bar set up.
label: human

text: Every square inch of the interior is covered in layers of stickers and spray paint, giving it a raw, unpolished charm that simply cannot be manufactured. If you are looking for a sanitized, corporate club experience with bottle service and velvet ropes, you have definitely come to the wrong place. However, for those who value musical history and a genuine underground spirit, this legendary dive is an absolute local treasure. The stage is small and the room often gets cramped and hot, creating an intimate connection between the performers and the crowd that larger venues lack. You can practically feel the energy of the iconic bands that graced this tiny stage long before they became household names. The drinks are affordably priced, the staff is refreshingly no-nonsense, and the sound quality is surprisingly punchy for such a weathered building. Do not let the rough exterior or the industrial surroundings deter you, as the community inside is incredibly welcoming to true music fans.
label: llm

text: I'm quite easy to please food wise so this experience was a surprise to me. This restaurant is relatively pricey so perhaps my expectations were high based on what I perceived would be value for my dollar. nnWe dined on a surprisingly quiet Friday night. Even so, the service was adequate - nothing more, nothing less. Not very friendly and welcoming, just adequate. nnAs for the food. We started with the blue crab fondue served with french baguette toasts, which was absolutely fabulous. I'd definitely recommend this dish but don't eat too much or you'll have no room left for the entrees to come. nnEntrees were ribeye with roquefort cheese sauce, and my companion ordered the petit filet mignon. Sides are ordered separately; we selected grilled asparagus and potato gratin. The portions are quite generous but the presentation was way off for me. My ribeye arrived on a big plate with a large portion of roquefort smeared across the top, looking quite lonely without something (anything) to make it look appealing. Yes, I know the sides are served separately so that limits how the dish might be displayed, but more could have been done to appeal to the eye. nnAll in all, the food was adequate (except the delicious fondue! ). But I expected a much better experience for the price. I don't mind spending money to go out and have a delicious meal and lovely experience. But I do expect just that - a delicious meal and a lovely experience.
label: human

text: The ambiance initially seemed promising with its modern decor and soft lighting, but the experience went downhill almost immediately after we were seated. It took nearly twenty minutes for a server to even acknowledge our presence, let alone offer us water or a drink menu. When the waiter finally arrived, he seemed rushed and uninterested in providing any recommendations or explaining the daily specials. We started with the calamari, which arrived lukewarm and had a rubbery texture that suggested it had been sitting under a heat lamp for too long. The dipping sauce lacked any real flavor, tasting more like plain tomato paste than a zesty marinara. For the main course, I ordered the sea bass, expecting a fresh and delicate dish given the restaurant’s reputation for seafood. Unfortunately, the fish was incredibly overcooked and dry, crumbling apart with every forkful rather than flaking naturally. The accompanying vegetable medley was drowning in a greasy butter sauce that completely overpowered the natural taste of the produce. My partner’s steak was equally underwhelming, as it was served medium-well despite her specific request for it to be prepared medium-rare. To make matters worse, the noise level in the dining room became unbearable as the night progressed, making conversation nearly impossible. We tried to flag down our server to address the issues with our entrees, but he was nowhere to be found for a significant portion of the meal.
label: llm

text: After a failed attempt to eat at a local hotspot I re-check my Yelp bookmarks and voila! There's Cuisine Malaya, all the way across downtown Charlotte. I hoof it over about a mile and show up at this basic and simple cafe. Inside, the space is big and I'm hungry. All that walking has worked up an appetite and bonus, there's a check-in special for a free glass of wine or beer, woohoo! nnI order up a bunch of Malaysian items and they all please. One roti canai, one Malaysian chili shrimp and a peanut pancake for dessert. All well prepared, tasty, spicy and overall yummy! Service is really spot on and the price is right. Cuisine Malaya also serves up Japanese-sushi but I'd stick with the Malaysian. Cause it was good! So rock on Cuisine Malaya, you were worth the walk and thanks for the vino.. .
label: human

text: Score 1 for Yelp! I was in a real bind when my kitchen sink started leaking uncontrollably late on a Tuesday night. After calling three other plumbers who didn’t pick up, I decided to give this local business a try based on their high ratings. The technician arrived within thirty minutes of my call, which was much faster than I ever expected. He was incredibly professional and immediately identified that a rusted pipe was the culprit. Instead of trying to upsell me on a whole new system, he offered a quick and affordable fix that worked perfectly. The pricing was transparent from the start, so there were no nasty surprises when it came time to pay. I was also impressed by how clean he left the workspace, making sure to wipe down the cabinets and floor. It is rare to find such reliable service these days, especially on such short notice.
label: llm

text: I chose this hotel as part of a package on Travelocity. nnLocated uptown right near the Johnson and Wales campus, this hotel fit the bill. nnRoughly a mile from the center of Downtown and the Convention Center, the location is far enough to be out of the hustle and bustle but near enough to walk to the Convention Center and Downtown restaurants if you choose to do so. nnThe room on the second floor was smallish, but adequate. Safe in room, but other than that, no in room bling. Not a fan of the open shower at all. I like a nice shower with good water pressure. The shower in this room has a seat and a hand held shower head. It's not enclosed and there is no tub. To be fair, the shower head is on a mount that can be adjusted for height and direction, but the result is less than adequate water pressure. Any more and you would flood the bathroom. nnStaff is very friendly and helpful. Check in was uneventful and you can check out via the phone in your room. Final bill is shoved under your room door on the morning of your check out. nnBar/Restaurant is typical. Overpriced, but you have other choices. Dining options immediately around the hotel are limited. Subway, The Great Wok, Cedar Street Tavern are within short walking distance and are fine if you don't want or need to go downtown for better dining. nnThere is a CVS and a Harris Teeter also within short walking distance. nnParking is $13 a day in a structure next to the hotel. In room internet is $9. 95 for 24 hours. I understand a parking charge, but it seems a bit steep. I simply do not understand any hotel charging for Wi-Fi access in room when it's free in the lobby and other public spaces of the hotel. nnMinor quibbles, but If I were attending a multi-day conference at the Convention Center, I'd look for a hotel closer. Price would be close to a wash and convenience would be better.
label: human

text: Desperate for a place to stay, I broadened my search to the surrounding suburbs. I eventually found a room at a boutique inn located about fifteen minutes from the downtown area. The booking process over the phone was incredibly straightforward and the clerk was very sympathetic to my situation. Upon arriving at the property, I was immediately struck by the charming exterior and well-maintained landscaping. Check-in took less than five minutes, which was a relief after a long day of travel. The lobby smelled faintly of lavender and the air conditioning was a welcome reprieve from the humid North Carolina heat. My room was situated on the third floor, offering a quiet view of the courtyard below. I was pleasantly surprised by how spacious and modern the interior felt compared to the photos online. The king-sized bed was exceptionally comfortable, featuring high-quality linens and plenty of plush pillows. A large desk area provided the perfect space for me to catch up on work emails before the morning sessions. I also appreciated the high-speed internet, which never lagged during my stay. The bathroom was spotless, stocked with premium toiletries and thick, fluffy towels. Every morning, the hotel offered a complimentary breakfast buffet that exceeded my expectations. There were hot options like scrambled eggs and sausage, along with fresh fruit and artisanal pastries. The coffee was surprisingly good, which is a rare find in most mid-range hotels. Since I didn't have a car, I relied on a local shuttle service to get to the Charlotte Convention Center. The drivers were always punctual and gave me great tips on where to eat for dinner. One evening, I decided to dine at the hotel’s small on-site bistro. The menu was limited, but the burger I ordered was cooked to perfection. I spent a little time by the pool one afternoon, and it was a peaceful way to unwind.
label: llm

text: Now every time I go, the smell of the place takes me back (something between wood-fired kitchen and just.. . kitchen). nnThis is another relatively safe place I can go with my parents. Though their veggie options are scant, their veggie burger is made in-house, I can get their six cheese penne without bacon, and I've always enjoyed their pimento cheese dip. nnUnfortunately, I found little to eat for lunch yesterday. I was looking for something light, and save ordering a salad (sans meat, of course), there wasn't much else on the menu that appealed to me. I do love a good bowl of soup, but Harper's rarely has a veggie soup on tap, and yesterday was no different. I ordered the spinach quesadilla, hoping it would be more spinachy than cheesy and thinking it's hard to eff up a quesadilla. Right? nnWHAT a disappointment. The quesadilla was a total mess, stuffed to the brim with a slurpy cheese mixture. The filling was incredibly uneven - one triangle had cheese with just a hint of spinach, another was filled entirely with the spinach mixture (which I am 99% sure is just their spinach dip repurposed), and another had a surprising number of cold, mealy tomato cubes. nnPer the usual, my dad ordered a small cup of soup, and the server barely hid her disdain at our tiny order. The sneer was palpable. nnI think I'm done with Harper's for a while.
label: human

text: Returning there last week for dinner felt like stepping into a hazy, slightly modernized time capsule. The mahogany bar still gleams with that same polished elegance, though the faces behind it have certainly grown much younger. I remember the frantic energy of the dinner rush, balancing heavy trays of crab cakes and chilled martinis while trying to keep my composure. The menu has evolved since my days as a server, incorporating more contemporary ingredients like truffle oil and local microgreens. However, the signature shepherd’s pie remains a comforting staple that tastes exactly as I remember it. Our server was attentive and polite, possessing that familiar blend of professionalism and charm that the establishment has always required. We started with the calamari, which was fried to a perfect golden crisp and served with a zesty lemon aioli. The main courses arrived promptly, and my partner’s steak frites were cooked to a flawless medium-rare. The lighting remains dim and intimate, making it the perfect spot for a quiet conversation amidst the background hum of the crowd. I noticed that the old portrait in the foyer has been replaced by a piece of abstract art, which felt a bit jarring given the traditional vibe. Despite that minor décor change, the overall soul of the place seems remarkably intact. The wine list has expanded significantly, offering a diverse selection that caters to both casual drinkers and true connoisseurs.
label: llm

text: Simple layout, screens at every turn updating flight status, and overall a clean facility. nnI had no problems when checking in for a flight. TSA staff were extremely gentle and handled me with care, I walked out of there with no pain or discomfort. But in all seriousness, security check was your typical long delay, but its to be expected for an international airport. Once I got past security, I was able to find my gate with no problem. nnThe Enterprise shuttle ran every five to ten minutes, which is very convenient when in a hurry. Although i didn't use the pick up or drop off lanes, they seemed to be running smooth with no delays, my shuttle was able to  get through with relative ease. nnSimple layout, modern facility, customer service was good. Overall, I wouldn't mind flying back through this airport in the future.
label: human

text: The check-in process was surprisingly efficient, even with the long lines during peak hours. Security staff were professional, though they could definitely benefit from a bit more patience when dealing with first-time travelers. Once past the gates, the terminal layout felt intuitive enough that I didn't need to consult a map every five minutes. There are plenty of seating options near the gates, which is a relief compared to some of the more cramped hubs I've visited. Food choices are standard for a major facility, offering everything from quick snacks to sit-down meals at expectedly high prices. The cleanliness of the restrooms was acceptable, though a more frequent maintenance schedule would certainly be appreciated. Wi-Fi connectivity stayed strong throughout my three-hour layover, allowing me to get some work done without interruption.
label: llm

text: nnI was unimpressed with the customer service: the server was apparently not typically on the floor as she was the bartender. My first question is "Why? " She got our order incorrect (which actually ended up being a good thing) but was a bit slow. I usually like all salads but I did NOT like the chopped salad. For some reason, the acidity was too high and some of the flavors did not bode well together. nnMy friends raved about the Nutella pie: it was good but it was much more like a Cheesecake Factory cheesecake slice than a pie: huge and don't order more than one per table--too much. For dinner, we ordered the Pollo Bianco and since we both wanted it, we decided for family style. The family style doesn't come with side dishes so you have to order those separately--so we did. But then they brought the single serving and still brought the sides--and the single serving is served on top of mashed potatoes: one of the sides we ordered. Enter double sides of mashed potatoes. I will say the sauce of the chicken was good, but the mashed potatoes were the same as anywhere else. nnI guess it's just another standard chain restaurant. Too bad. It could have been so much more.
label: human

text: Usually, I find the heavy reliance on carbs and red sauces to be a bit overwhelming and repetitive for my palate. However, after hearing several friends rave about this local gem, I decided to give it a fair chance. The atmosphere was the first thing that struck me, as it felt more like a sophisticated bistro than a typical checkered-tablecloth joint. We started our meal with the grilled octopus, which was perfectly charred and incredibly tender. For the main course, I stepped out of my comfort zone and ordered the homemade pappardelle with a wild mushroom ragu. To my surprise, the pasta was exceptionally light and had a delicate texture that seemed to melt in my mouth. The sauce wasn't the heavy, salty mess I usually dread, but rather a complex and earthy blend of flavors. My companion ordered the pan-seared sea bass, which arrived with a perfectly crispy skin and a moist, flaky center. Even the wine pairing suggested by our knowledgeable server was spot on, enhancing the meal without being overpowering. I particularly appreciated that the portions were sensible, leaving us feeling satisfied rather than uncomfortably stuffed. For dessert, we shared a lemon polenta cake that provided a refreshing, citrusy finish to a wonderful evening.
label: llm

text: nnIts been more that 8 years since, I had been to a themepark (Kennywood, Pittsburgh, PA),  so I wasn't sure how I would feel about riding the rides, and doing the carnival theme activities. nnWe opted for the evening passes (starting at 4PM), since we both knew a full-day would have been too much for us. nnFirst parking is a joke and a crime. They force you to pay to park to be able to go into the park. This isn't just for premium parking, but its for general too. This is just another way to rake the park goers over the coals. Having to pay to park, really made me not ever want to come back here. nnAs for rides, we focused mainly on Rollercoaster, and wanted to get as many of them as possible. The Eliminator (Nascar theme and biggest in the park) was fun, fast, and rough. You experience at a lot of G's and airtime on this ride, but my head paid the price and was rattled. Afterburn had to be my favorite of the day, but we experienced a big delay due to someone getting sick on the ride. We finished the night with Nighthawk, and waited inline for about 1. 5 hrs. It was a really fun ride, but not sure if it was worth the "wait 1 min for 1 seconded of riding" ratio. nnThe rest of the rides were entertaining, no other great recommendations. nnThe park was crowded on a the Saturday night, but not painful to move around through the park. Everyone was friendly having a good night out. nnSome of the bathrooms were really old and disgusting. nnFood was expensive and not that awesome. We missed a deal were we could have got a full pizza for $11 dollars, but the staff didn't inform us and sold us 2 slices for $9 instead. nnOverall, it filled in a slot in a a empty evening, but I think I have either grown out of themeparks or this one just didn't do a go job of re-instilling the magic of them.
label: human

text: The layout is sprawling, requiring a fair amount of walking between the main attractions. Wait times can be quite daunting, often exceeding two hours for the most popular rides. If you have small children, you will find the lack of shaded seating areas rather frustrating during the midday heat. The food options are standard fairground quality, though the prices certainly suggest a more gourmet experience. I found the animatronics to be slightly dated, lacking the fluidity of more modern park technology. However, the attention to detail in the gift shops is surprisingly impressive and thematic. Staff members are generally polite, though they seem overwhelmed by the massive weekend crowds. One of the highlights is the evening light show, which utilizes state-of-the-art projection mapping on the central castle. The soundtrack throughout the park is catchy, but it tends to loop a bit too frequently for comfort. Many of the interactive elements were out of order during my particular visit, which was a disappointment. If you are a fan of lore, you will appreciate the deep backstory woven into the queues. For the casual visitor, the high price of admission might feel like a steep barrier to entry. Parking is another logistical hurdle, as the shuttle buses run on an inconsistent schedule. I would recommend arriving at least thirty minutes before the gates open to maximize your time. The mobile app is supposed to help with navigation, but it drained my phone battery within a few hours. Some of the thrill rides are genuinely exhilarating, offering drops that will leave your stomach in your throat. Yet, the overall pacing of the park feels disjointed, with long gaps between major points of interest. Safety protocols are strictly enforced, which provides a welcome sense of security for families.
label: llm

text: Depending on your sobriety level when you leave, it may be because you have a little trouble remembering your time there. nnWhen you enter past the surly ticket takers and go through the doors you're greeted by the booming music of top 40s remixes, though I do like the fact that they don't play it so loud that you can't hear someone screaming in your ear. The drinks here are kinda eh, you don't get much for your money and they are fairly weak in my opinion. Though I hear that on Sunday well drinks are free with a $10 cover, and Fridays offers free beer on tap so that's something to keep in mind. nnThe main reason to go here is for the dancing! They have a huge dance floor and it is quite a sight to see everyone dancing their tushes off! I was particularly amused by the twink who was twerkin it like it ain't no thang! I always have a fun time here, even when I'm the DD. The patio outside is filled with people smoking and chatting each other up. Good if you'd like to have a conversation with someone you've met, not so good if you are adverse to cigarette smoke though. nnScorpio's is a fun time, and they have lots of cool drag shows that are pretty awesome to watch. There is a fair mix of people on most days. It is extremely ghetto on Saturday though, and lots of fights break out on that day though so I'd steer away from that day.
label: human

text: This place is pretty hard to review. On one hand, the atmosphere is absolutely enchanting with its dim lighting and vintage decor. On the other hand, the service was so slow that we almost considered leaving before our appetizers arrived. The menu offers an eclectic mix of fusion dishes that look incredible on paper. However, the execution of the main course left something to be desired in terms of seasoning. My partner’s steak was cooked to a perfect medium-rare, yet my pasta was noticeably overcooked and mushy. We were also surprised by the pricing, which felt a bit steep for the portion sizes provided. Despite these inconsistencies, the cocktail list is genuinely one of the most creative I have seen in the city. The "Smoky Orchard" drink was a highlight of the night, blending flavors I never thought would work together. The staff members were incredibly polite, though they seemed overwhelmed by the Friday night rush. It is the kind of spot where you might have the best meal of your life or a mediocre experience depending on the day. If you value ambiance and drinks over a consistent dining experience, you will likely enjoy your time here. I am still debating whether I would return for a second visit or try somewhere new. Ultimately, your enjoyment will depend entirely on what you prioritize in a night out.
label: llm

text: The wait staff was nice - that's the only reason I gave then two stars instead of one. We should have known to skip this place when we saw the cheesy plastic sign and neon logo, but we decided to give it a chance. Our waitress asked if we wanted to sit somewhere quiet or not (which was considerate), but when we said we'd like a quiet spot, we ended up gitting a table right next to some annoying doorbell thing that gave three loud beeps every time someone walked into or out of the door, so we asked to be moved. We were also given lunch instead of dinner menus, so we had to ask for the right menus. When we finally ordered and got our food, the quantity and price looked okay, but the quality was seriously lacking. The duck in the duck spring roll seemed to be prepared well, but there were none of the other subtle ingredients and flavors that one would expect - no rice noodles, carrots, mint, basil, ect. - just iceberg lettuce and cucumber! And the dipping sauce was overly thick, way too sweet and tasted like something that came out of a jar. The wonton soup broth was bland and oily, and the wontons were okay but tasted like something I could get out of a box from the frozen section of a store. The pineapple fried rice was okay, but didn't have as much chicken or pineapple as we would have expected, the chicken was a bit dry and again - none of the subtle flavors that we're used to in this dish that make it so tasty - cilantro, raisins, cashews, ect. The beef rendeng was terrible - a pile of beef bits in a disgusting looking sauce with a side of unseasoned brocoli and cold canned pineapple. The sauce actually had a decent flavor, but it looked so unappetizing and the beef was so dry that I sent it back. The waiter took the amount of the bill, so we were grateful for that.
label: human

text: My experience was the complete opposite of what I expected based on the high rating. From the moment we walked in, the atmosphere felt chaotic and unwelcoming. The hostess didn't even acknowledge us for five minutes, despite the fact that the foyer was nearly empty. Once we were finally seated, the table was visibly sticky and had crumbs from the previous guests. We waited another twenty minutes just for someone to bring us water and take our drink orders. When the food finally arrived, it was lukewarm at best and lacked any discernible seasoning. I ordered the signature pasta dish, but the sauce tasted like it came straight out of a cheap tin can. My partner’s steak was overcooked to the point of being rubbery, despite asking for it medium-rare. When we tried to flag down our server to address the issues, they consistently avoided eye contact. To make matters worse, the prices are astronomical for the quality of the ingredients being used. I have had better meals at fast-food chains for a quarter of the cost. text: nnI know it's hard to imagine hating a place where someone else has picked up the tab. text: Back then, I always associated the dim lighting and heavy mahogany furniture with long, drawn-out spreadsheets and awkward small talk. text: We stopped in about an hour before close on a Saturday night and the place was surprisingly empty. text: Upon entering, the decor felt somewhat dated and the lighting was a bit too dim for comfort. text: nnThe entertainment (Lizzy Ross Band) was phenomenal. I mean, absolutely mind-blowing. text: I'm torn. On one hand, the atmosphere at the restaurant is undeniably electric, capturing a vibe that few places in the city can match. text: nnCharlotte Douglas is a major air hub, and you certainly won't forget it - it's absolutely jam packed with people on a perpetual basis, be it 3 AM or 9 PM. Lines for food become cumbersome and scary to the point where I've foregone breakfast just to avoid the wait. text: However, that is a bar so low you would need a shovel to find it. The carpet looks like it was salvaged from a 1970s bowling alley that specialized in heavy smokers. text: I have a confession to make and it won't be pretty.. . I stayed away from this blockbuster for months because the hype felt suffocatingly dense. The cinematography was undeniably breathtaking, but pretty pictures cannot compensate for a hollow soul. Every character felt like a cardboard cutout designed to deliver heavy-handed metaphors rather than genuine human emotion. I wanted to root for the protagonist, yet their motivations remained as murky as the film's dark color palette. Critics are calling this a revolutionary achievement in filmmaking, but to me, it felt like an exercise in self-indulgence. The three-hour runtime was an absolute test of my patience that I unfortunately failed halfway through. I even tried to re-watch the second half the next day, thinking perhaps I was just in a bad mood. Sadly, the experience was even more grating the second time around. There is a fine line between "slow-burn" and "glacial," and this film crossed it within the first act.

text: We chose this spot because it was conveniently located right across from the cinema. Upon entering, we were immediately greeted by a friendly hostess who seated us in a cozy corner booth. The food arrived much faster than we expected, which was great since we were on a bit of a schedule. The potato skins were cooked to perfection, with just the right amount of melted cheese and crispy bacon bits. They came with a side of sour cream that tasted incredibly fresh and tangy. Next, we dove into the cauliflower wings, which had a fantastic kick to them without being overwhelmingly hot. The breading was light and crunchy, providing a satisfying texture in every single bite. We both agreed that the house-made ranch dipping sauce provided the perfect cooling balance to the spice. Throughout the meal, our server checked on us a couple of times to ensure everything was to our liking. Even though the restaurant was starting to get busy, we never felt rushed or ignored by the staff. The portion sizes were surprisingly generous for appetizers, leaving us feeling perfectly satisfied but not overly full. We also noticed how clean and well-maintained the dining area was, which is always a major plus. When the bill came, we were pleasantly surprised at how affordable the total was for such high-quality food. We paid quickly and had plenty of time to walk over to the theater without having to run. text: nnDrinks: Had a guy who grew up in Napa picking wines so we had a few very wonderful bottles. He was impressed with the restaurant's selection and we were with his. I also had a microbrew amber ale on draft that was wonderful. nService: Was not over or underdone. Had the flair and attention of a nice establishment without being too snobby/formal. One bottle of wine we particularly liked ran out so the manager came over to talk about similar choices. Nice touch. nAppetizers: Choosing cheese and then pairing them with membrio, walnuts and bread was lovely. The house bread with butter mixed with kalamata olives was a wonderful touch. The calamari rivaled your favorite sports bar (I expected better). The Flavors of the Mediterranean plate was good but not extraordinary. It was a nice option from standard fare for certain though. nMain meal: For the price we each agreed we didn't get anything special. Certainly the seasonal Jumbo Scallops on Risotto was good, but it wasn't lovely. Almost too salty and there was nothing tying the seafood with the grain. And I adore both items. The Bolognese was described as 'eh' and 'standard' and the two who got the pork roasts were equally so-so in review and description. nAtmosphere: A jazz trio started up as we ate and it added a light and fun atmosphere to the experience. Tables around us were in good spirits, the lighting was set just right and there was enough space to move between tables (very uncommon in SF). It was nice. nnConclusion: This was a good experience but not great. I don't want to think because this is a smaller town then I'm used to, "nice" local places  = lower standards. I tend more to think there were good ideas here not executed to their fullest. 3 stars is all about the food which is ultimately why we pay these prices and go to these places. I think if the ingredients were fresher and the temperatures and spices were watched closer then this could be a 5 star no matter in what city it's located.

text: So needless to say I had high hopes for Mert's. nnI went with the buttermilk and herb chicken fingers which sounded incredible. They were about $11 and came with two sides. text: Finding a place that does all three with genuine heart can be a challenge, especially in a city far from the Mason-Dixon line. However, this local gem managed to transport my taste buds straight to a cozy porch in Georgia from the moment I walked through the door. The aroma of sizzling batter and buttermilk yeast hitting the air was enough to make my mouth water instantly. I started with the fried chicken, which arrived with a crust so crisp it shattered perfectly with every bite. Beneath that golden exterior, the meat remained incredibly juicy and seasoned all the way to the bone. It wasn't overly greasy, which is a rare feat for poultry this deeply fried and satisfying. Next came the biscuits and gravy, a dish that I usually find either too salty or too bland elsewhere. Here, the biscuits were tall, flaky, and buttery enough to melt without much effort. The sausage gravy was thick and peppery, boasting large chunks of savory meat that tied everything together. Even the side of collard greens had a smoky depth that suggested they had been simmering for hours. I appreciated that the service was just as warm as the food, with the staff treating every guest like an old family friend. After such a heavy meal, I wasn't sure if I had room for dessert, but I simply couldn't pass up the banana pudding. It was served in a generous mason jar, layered with fresh slices of fruit and plenty of vanilla wafers. The custard was silky and light, providing the perfect sweet finish to a very savory afternoon. Every spoonful felt like a nostalgic hug, even for someone who didn't have a Southern grandmother to make it for them. I left the restaurant feeling completely satisfied and already planning which friends I would bring back next weekend.

text: It was a nightmare. First and foremost, they were serving a limited, special event menu. Walking in, you are immediately greeted by a professional staff that prioritizes clear communication and ensures every client feels comfortable with their design choice. The studio itself is impeccably clean, maintaining the highest safety standards while still feeling like a creative sanctuary rather than a sterile office. It is no surprise that their appointment books fill up so quickly, as the level of craftsmanship here is truly unparalleled in the Charlotte area. Whether you are a seasoned collector or a first-timer looking for something small, the team treats every project with the same degree of respect and dedication. Fu’s Custom Tattoo has firmly cemented itself as a cornerstone of the local arts scene and is undoubtedly the premier destination for high-quality ink in the city.
label: llm

text: nnI came in to transfer service from my roommate's name into my name, since she was moving out. It was about 3: 00 on a Monday. I was lucky enough to be first in line, but 10 or so people quickly lined up behind me while we waited. There were only 4 employees working, and one of them, after glaring up to see the forming line, left for a break, and was in no hurry to get back. nnI explained why I was there and presented my modem, and was informed that I would have to start a new account instead of transferring, since I didn't have written permission from my roommate. Ok, no big deal. The lady helping my was cordial, but unfriendly and bored out of her mind. She talked to the computer screen instead of to my face. After starting my new account, she watched me pack up my modem, router, and all it's cables and start to walk away, before she asked if I would like go ahead and pay the first month so I wouldn't be billed for it. Good thing my wallet was at the bottom of my purse, under all the equipment she just watched me put on top of it! nnI know working with the public can be trying, and no one likes Mondays, but I hope I never have problems with my service that involve a visit back to the office. Talk about unpleasant.

text: I walked into the local branch to swap out an old modem, and the atmosphere was heavier than a lead blanket. The woman who greeted me didn't even look up from her screen, emitting a sigh that felt like it carried the weight of a thousand technical support tickets. I tried to offer a friendly "hello," but it was met with a stare so vacant I genuinely wondered if she was a hologram. Every movement she made was painstakingly slow, as if clicking a mouse button required an immense physical sacrifice. To her left, another representative was explaining a billing discrepancy to an elderly man with all the enthusiasm of someone reading a legal disclaimer. It’s almost impressive how they’ve managed to curate a staff that possesses zero percent of the "service" part of customer service. I understand that dealing with disgruntled callers all day is soul-crushing, but the in-person vibe is just next-level misery. It makes me feel like I’m an inconvenience just by existing in their lobby for five minutes. Even the fluorescent lighting seemed to be flickering in sympathy with their collective despair. Eventually, I got my new equipment handed to me without a single word being exchanged during the entire transaction. I left the building feeling like I needed a shower and a hug just to shake off that oppressive aura.
label: llm

text: nnIt's just ok in my opinion. I had a combo platter when I came: beef ribs, fried catfish, collards, and Mac and cheese. The beef ribs were not quite what I was expecting or really would have ordered if I had known. They were the short kind - and in this case, emphasis on short. There was very little meat on them. The BBQ sauce was too vinegary for my tastes, just ok. The catfish was solid, but again, when I was eating it I still didn't understand the hype. The collards were the best part of the meal (delicious take on a classic), and the Mac and cheese was good too, though under seasoned. nnMy partner had the salmon cakes, which were very good. I don't remember what else she had, but this aspect was memorable and quite good. nnWe both had cake for dessert, which again were good but not outstanding. nnThe atmosphere is cool here. I like the bright colors and the VERY friendly and courteous wait staff. You can tell they want their customers to be happy, but the food just wasn't that great, so I can't go above 3 stars for now. We may try mert's again, so we'll see.

text: Walking into the restaurant, the atmosphere felt incredibly warm and welcoming, just like a classic Southern diner should be. The wait time on a Saturday afternoon was a bit long, but we decided to stay since the delicious smells coming from the kitchen were irresistible. Once we were seated, our server greeted us with a genuine smile and immediately recommended their famous cornbread to start the meal. When the basket arrived, the cornbread was moist, buttery, and had just the right amount of sweetness to satisfy any craving. For my main course, I opted for the fried chicken, which came out golden brown and perfectly seasoned. The meat was juicy and tender, proving why this place has such a stellar reputation in the Queen City. My partner ordered the salmon cakes, and they were packed with fresh flavor without being overly breaded or greasy. As for the sides, the collard greens had a wonderful smoky depth that tasted like they had been simmering for hours. The macaroni and cheese was another standout, featuring a rich, creamy sauce and a perfect baked crust on top.
label: llm

text: They know this so I get a call every year inviting me back and who am I to say no? From the minute you walk into the restaurant to the time you leave it's like they put these rose colored glasses on you and all you see is the awesome atmosphere, service, and food. nWe received 2 complimentary glasses of champagne, and prosciutto wrapped arracini to start us off. Lobster & Crab Cakes for sweetie and a tomato mozzarella salad for me. The tomatoes were cut thick and were complimented by sweet cherry tomatoes and a 12 year aged balsamic. All very well done. I admit that I did make a mistake. I wanted to save room for dessert, so I usually order the porcini rubbed delmonico, but I figured a bone in steak was a bit much. I ordered the 10 Oz Fillet instead and it was served with 2 large shrimp stuffed with lump crabmeat. The fillet was cooked nicely and the shrimp were prepared to my satisfaction, I just prefer a ribeye, so looking back I should order what I like and have the mindset to take home what I can't finish. Now, onto the side dishes.. . the Lobster Mac N Cheese is like heaven on a plate, I don't know or do I particularly care how much butter they add to it, but it is nothing short of spectacular. Creamed Spinach is also awesome. Cheesecake for dessert was like it came out of a magazine. I think someone told me that their Head Chef was a pastry chef in his past life which leads me to believe that their cheesecake at this location is better than most. nThe service at the Capital Grille is top notch. They take such good care of you and make you feel like you're the only customer. I will continue to go back for this reason and encourage everyone to do the same. nnSee you soon Guys!

text: Each time, the experience seems to get better than the last. This year, the staff went above and beyond to make my evening feel truly special. As soon as we walked through the doors, the hostess greeted me with a warm "Happy Birthday" and led us to a beautifully decorated table. There were even shimmering birthday confetti pieces scattered across the white tablecloth. Our server was attentive without being overbearing, which I always appreciate in a high-end steakhouse. We started the meal with the pan-fried calamari with hot cherry peppers, and it was perfectly crispy. For the main course, I opted for the bone-in ribeye, cooked to a flawless medium-rare. My partner ordered the seared citrus glazed salmon, which was light yet incredibly flavorful. The side of lobster mac and cheese is an absolute must-order every single time we visit. We also shared the grilled asparagus, which had a lovely char and just the right amount of crunch. Throughout the meal, the manager stopped by our table to ensure everything was to our satisfaction. It is this level of personal attention that keeps us coming back year after year. The wine list is extensive, and the sommelier helped us pick a perfect Cabernet to pair with our steaks. For dessert, they surprised me with their signature cheesecake topped with fresh berries. It was rich, creamy, and came with a candle for me to make a wish. The atmosphere remained sophisticated yet comfortable, making it the perfect setting for a celebration. Even though the restaurant was busy, we never felt rushed to finish our meal. I honestly cannot think of a single thing I would change about the entire night. I am already looking forward to celebrating my birthday here again next year.
label: llm

text: So disclaimer first, I would prefer a bar with a small dance floor over a large club with seizure inducing strobe lights any day. Yes guys, there are plenty of young girls here. It isn't difficult to find several packs of half-drunk girls to grind on, and if you lack confidence to approach at least the bartenders are gorgeous. This is the perfect place to find someone to take home, and it's so loud you don't have to worry about all the dumb things you say. Truthfully though it's just not my scene. I don't won't to sound pretentious, but this place feels dirty and you will most likely step in vomit or at least spilled beer. As others have said, it's mostly hip-hop, when I was there I rarely heard any house or trance. The crowd definitely trends younger, mostly in their teens or low 20s. I'm 25 and I almost felt too old there. But maybe that says more about me than it does Bar Charlotte. For that reason, I can't give this place less than two stars. Just know what you're getting into, it's your typical teenage get drunk and go nuts kind of club. That could be just what you're looking for. But the $15 cover on a Friday night is steep, and for me it just wasn't worth it.

text: The product arrived in minimalist packaging, which I appreciated for its environmental considerations. Setup was straightforward, taking roughly ten minutes from unboxing to full operation. Regarding the design, the aesthetic is modern and fits well into most home office environments. However, the materials used for the outer casing feel somewhat cheaper than the marketing photos suggested. Performance is generally reliable, with the internal processor handling multitasking without any significant lag. I did encounter a persistent issue where the cooling fan became quite loud during intensive tasks. The screen resolution is crisp, making it a joy to use for both work and media consumption. Conversely, the keyboard travel is quite shallow, which might bother those used to mechanical keys. Battery longevity is average, lasting through a typical workday but requiring a charge by early evening. Software updates have been frequent, suggesting the manufacturer is committed to long-term support. One standout feature is the port selection, which includes everything a professional might need without adapters. The price point is slightly higher than competitors, but the build consistency justifies some of that cost.
label: llm

text: I love their big, plush chairs. I love their aisles and aisles of books. Won't stop me from coming back, but I never expect much. nnOh! And I completely agree with the parking trouble that other Yelpers have.. . Good luck.

text: The atmosphere is always so welcoming and provides a perfect escape from the hustle and bustle of daily life. I particularly appreciate how organized the shelves are, making it easy to find both new releases and obscure classics. The staff members are consistently helpful and seem genuinely passionate about the books they recommend. I often find myself spending hours wandering through the aisles, discovering titles I never would have found online. Their selection of stationery and journals is also impressive, often featuring high-quality brands that are hard to find elsewhere. The in-store café is a wonderful touch, offering a quiet place to preview a potential purchase while enjoying a treat. I have spent many rainy afternoons tucked away in a corner with a latte and a thick novel. The children’s section is vibrant and engaging, which makes it a great place to foster a love for reading in younger generations. While the prices can be higher than those of online retailers, the experience of browsing in person is worth the extra few dollars.

text: The moment I stepped inside, a wave of stale fryer oil and mildew hit me like a physical blow. text: Sorry honey, it's true. text: He requires premium fuel in the form of artisanal coffee and craft beer just to function correctly in the morning. His "maintenance fees" include a subscription to every sports package available, which he claims is essential for his overall mental well-being. I recently discovered that his hobby of "collecting tools" actually means buying industrial-grade saws for home projects he rarely finishes. Even his wardrobe has evolved from simple t-shirts to high-end performance gear that he wears mostly to sit on the couch. Despite the high price tag, the build quality is surprisingly durable and he handles heavy lifting with impressive ease. He comes with a built-in heater function that is perfect for cold winter nights, though he does tend to snore at a high decibel level. The emotional support software is top-tier, even if the "listening" feature sometimes glitches during the peak of football season. Shipping was relatively fast—we’ve been together for ten years now—but the return policy is non-existent at this point. I have occasionally considered trading him in for a more economical model, but the nostalgic value is simply too high to calculate.

text: nnAs in, less atmosphere, spottier service, but good deals and (in some cases) surprisingly good food. nnA complaint I often hear about Ethiopian is that it all tastes the same - whether that's actually true (I don't think so) or it's a result of our western minds being so used to each separate dish having, well, it's own, separate dish, that when it's all piled onto a delicious piece of Injera, the way we experience flavor shifts is a mystery to me. At Red Sea, there is no mistaking Wat for Alicha - the flavors in each dish (even just stewed lentils) are distinct. Some things are sweet - others salty. And there's none of this "spice level" stuff - you get the full range, when ordering a combo (at 10. 99, veggie combo is a steal). nnDings - nuked Sambusas. Service was both good (presence, smiles) and cranky (unhappiness about splitting a bill 3 ways, each portion on a card). Warm, as in tired A/C. But really good, thoughtfully prepared food. Lovely.

text: While Red Sea offers a more gritty, no-frills experience for the late-night crowd, Meskerem provides a polished and sophisticated alternative. The multi-level seating area, especially the sun-drenched top floor, creates an inviting ambiance that outshines its local competitors. You can immediately sense the difference in the service, which is attentive without being overbearing. As for the menu, the offerings reflect a commitment to high-quality ingredients and nuanced spice profiles. The kitfo is buttery and rich, prepared with a level of care that justifies the slightly higher price tag. Even the injera feels lighter and fresher here, serving as the perfect sponge for their vibrant vegetarian sampler. It is the kind of place where you feel comfortable bringing a date or hosting a business dinner. While some might argue that Red Sea has more "soul," there is no denying the consistency found at this Adams Morgan staple. The presentation of the meat platters is artful, turning a communal meal into a feast for the eyes as well as the palate.
label: llm

text: But, unfortunately, I had the worst sushi I've ever had at Fujo. nnWe split a salmon roll, a spicy tuna roll and a Godzilla roll. The salmon was too tough to be chewed. The Godzilla roll was yummy but not amazing - it was the most redeeming part of the meal for sure though. We also tried the sesame tofu and it was a huge disappointment - the tofu was so hard it was difficult to chew and it came with almost no veggies (4 tiny broccoli florets don't count). Our server was friendly and attentive and that's what's keeping this review from being a lower one. I didn't send anything back or complain to the server because it was a week night, we were tired, and we knew we wouldn't be back again. nnAll in all, it was def not my best groupon date night. Live and learn!

text: However, the meal I was served last night pushed my limits of tolerance to the absolute brink. text: No point talking about the food, y'all know what to expect. But what is unexpected is that there is a player piano in the front downstairs tinkling pleasant quasi-classical tunes. nnUp the circular staircase upstairs is wi-fi and cable news on a big screen at a tolerable level. I rarely ever want to go IN to a fast-food place because the environment is usually such a turn-off, but this location is a nice alternative. Unlike a previous reviewer, I found the place to be quite clean and this was at a very busy lunch time. nnGetting in is a bit of a trial as you have to cross through the drive-through line and the people in their cars are not really looking out for pedestrians. nnI'd return here for a place to linger a bit, which is a shocker when I think about it.

text: Instead of the usual plastic seating, you’ll find plush booths and sleek, modern decor throughout the space. Natural light floods through the floor-to-ceiling windows, creating a bright and welcoming environment for everyone. The employees here are exceptionally polite and often bring your meal directly to your table with a smile. Despite the more upscale feel of the building, the service remains lightning-fast and the food is served fresh. text: I definitely picked the right place for my birthday dinner. We showed up slightly early and got to mingle in the bar for a few minutes- what a fun bar! text: That was my immediate reaction the moment the first plate hit the table at this charming little bistro. The presentation alone was enough to make my mouth water, with vibrant colors and artful garnishes. I started with the truffle-infused mushroom risotto, which was creamy, rich, and cooked to absolute perfection. The earthy aroma filled the air, promising a flavor profile that did not disappoint. Every bite felt like a warm hug, offering a satisfying texture that balanced the tender grains with crisp parmesan tuiles. For the main course, the pan-seared sea bass was undeniably the star of the evening. The skin was incredibly crispy, while the delicate white fish underneath remained moist and flaky. It was served over a bed of lemon-scented asparagus that provided a refreshing zing to the palate. Beyond the food, the service was impeccable, with a staff that anticipated our every need without being intrusive. The soft lighting and jazz music playing in the background created a cozy, intimate atmosphere perfect for a date night. We paired our meal with a local Chardonnay that complemented the seafood beautifully. Even though we were stuffed, we couldn't resist splitting the molten lava cake for dessert. It was the perfect sweet ending to an already spectacular dining experience. If you are looking for a culinary gem that treats food like art, you simply must visit this place.

text: It arrived warm, crusty on the outside, and perfectly soft on the inside, accompanied by a decadent dipping oil that I couldn't stop eating. text: Where do I start. I suppose the hostess's complete lack of a greeting was the first red flag of the evening.
